topics.title: Foundations: superfluid medium, bulk arena, and throat defects
topics.summary: The model starts with a declared bulk superfluid arena, finite brane-bulk throat defects, and a parent action that fixes the fields used downstream.

physical_picture: The reader should begin with the physical objects rather than the PN outputs. The bulk is the ambient dynamical medium, the brane is the observed sector, and a particle is modeled as a finite throat-like defect connecting brane and bulk support structure.

This topic separates what is declared in the parent model from what is later obtained by projection or reduction. That distinction matters because many later results are exact only after a specified closure or controlled limit.
mathematical_core: The parent level uses a GNLS-type bulk sector together with localized electromagnetic degrees of freedom. The graph records this as the current declared parent action, not yet as the promoted moving-wall action.
The important reader-level invariant is provenance. Every later claim should say which parent object, projection, closure, or branch computation it depends on.
status_note: This page is backed by published 4D and ontology papers where available. Any moving-throat wall dynamics introduced later remains additive and must not be read back into the frozen parent paper unless a later paper explicitly adds it.

topics.title: Projection versus reduction: why the brane is an open subsystem
topics.summary: Projection defines what a brane observer measures; reduction is an extra controlled dynamical simplification and cannot be silently identified with projection.

physical_picture: A brane observer sees projected quantities, not the entire bulk state. The brane sector is therefore open: information, support, and boundary data can live outside the reduced brane description.
This is the conceptual reason later readouts must be treated carefully. A response packet is a measured or compressed output, not automatically a new physical throat object.
mathematical_core: The projection kernel gives an exact measurement definition. A zero-mode or brane-localized reduction is a separate approximation step with its own assumptions.
Public explanations should preserve this order: parent fields first, projection second, controlled reduction third, downstream claims last.
status_note: The graph contains an explicit firewall blocking the invalid shortcut "projection equals reduction." Public pages should keep that warning visible.

topics.title: Electromagnetism and charge bookkeeping
topics.summary: The electromagnetic sector has a controlled zero-mode Maxwell limit, but charge sign and coupling bookkeeping are not derived from throat circulation or geometry alone.

physical_picture: The EM story is intentionally split into a localized parent sector, a brane zero-mode limit, and charge-branch bookkeeping. That prevents older shorthand symbols from being mistaken for physical electric charge.
Magnetic or vortical circulation can be real structure without being the definition of electric charge sign.
mathematical_core: The safe public statement is a controlled Maxwell reduction in the zero-mode brane limit. Beyond that limit, mixed and transverse components must be tracked rather than erased.
The graph carries separate firewalls for charge sign, q_eff/q_star bookkeeping, and kappa_rho notation.
status_note: This topic is mostly paper-backed, but some mixed-sector moving-throat plumbing remains open and is handled in later pending topics.

topics.title: Post-Newtonian ladder: 1PN through 4PN
topics.summary: The published PN chain records exact 1PN, 2PN, and 3PN assemblies within declared closures, while 4PN is local/conditional because the inherited tail normalization remains open.

physical_picture: The PN ladder is best read as a sequence of increasingly strict matching claims. Lower-order conservative sectors are exact within their declared closure hierarchy; higher-order dissipative and tail sectors expose branch-output requirements.
This framing helps readers avoid an overclaim: a local algebraic match is not always the same as a solved physical branch.
mathematical_core: The key public math is the equality of the model's effective two-body Lagrangian with standard PN targets at each controlled stage.
The 4PN page should always point readers back to the 2.5PN quadrupole normalization gate, because that inherited gate is what blocks an unconditional full-tail theorem.
status_note: The frozen papers should remain fixed. If later work closes an open gate, the website should add a later-development section rather than rewrite the original PN status.

topics.title: Quadrupole radiation and the 2.5PN normalization gate
topics.summary: The 2.5PN sector narrows the dissipative problem to an outgoing quadrupole normalization target, but the actual branch data must still supply the normalization.

physical_picture: The quadrupole sector is where a reader sees the difference between narrowing a target and solving the physical branch. The outgoing port must deliver the right passive quadrupole response.
The model has strong structure here, but the status remains conditional until the same branch exports the normalization data without target fitting.
mathematical_core: The central target is an invariant product involving the source scale and outgoing response coefficient. The graph records it as EQ_P0_TARGET and protects it with open-gate status.
Exact angular source-map facts should not be upgraded into radial or axial normalization closure. That is why the angular-not-radial firewall belongs on the public page.
status_note: Published papers describe the conditional narrowing. Future work should add a closure paper or branch computation rather than mutate this status.

topics.title: Moving-throat PDE program
topics.summary: The moving-throat program studies wall/support dynamics, branch selection, and response export, but some parts are currently notes-backed rather than formal paper-backed.

physical_picture: This is the active bridge from a static or reduced throat picture to an executable physical branch. It asks which wall variables, material laws, and boundary packets the same branch must export.
The public page should be candid: much of this is organized and audited, but not all of it has a frozen formal paper yet.
mathematical_core: The wall PDE is exact only relative to the action that contains the wall term. The current parent action and the promoted parent action therefore need separate labels.
The branch exporter is the mathematical object that should eventually connect PDE solutions to PN and anomaly response packets.
status_note: Tag all notes-backed material here as paper pending. Once a PDE paper or ledger section is published, the source links can be backfilled without rewriting the topic's earlier claims.

topics.title: Branch response packets and target-blind export
topics.summary: The model needs branch data exported before comparison to PN or anomaly targets; response packets must be target-blind and downstream of the physical branch.

physical_picture: A response packet is the branch's exported data, not a physical object in its own right. That distinction keeps the comparison to target coefficients honest.
Packet A carries conservative/outgoing normalization data; Packet B carries orbit-lock or weak-axisymmetric data where relevant.
mathematical_core: The weak-form branch extractor is the planned interface between solved profiles and invariant packet data. It should output quantities such as K, M, B_n, Z_n, N_n, and grouped projectors without reading the target first.
This page should be treated as the public checklist for future executable branch solvers.
status_note: Most details are pending formal publication. The generated backfill list records exactly which note sources need replacement or citation once papers exist.

topics.title: 5PN continuation and full-bundle surface
topics.summary: The 5PN continuation organizes full-bundle targets, monomial quotients, and weak-axisymmetric transport, but it is presently a future-paper area.

physical_picture: The 5PN material is a continuation layer, not a frozen published endpoint. It packages a reduced full-bundle surface and identifies which branch-placement and even-gate conditions remain.
The reader should see this as a map of precise targets for future branch computation.
mathematical_core: The monomial quotient and Xi-style prefactor slope organize higher-order response structure. Those coordinates are useful, but they do not by themselves solve the full conservative even gates.
Public pages should keep the similarity/orbit theorem separate from full 5PN closure.
status_note: This page should be marked paper pending until the 5PN derivation is promoted from notes to a formal paper.

topics.title: Lepton and atom reduced sectors
topics.summary: Atom and lepton constructions currently live in reduced-sector and conditional corridors, with several pieces still awaiting formal papers.

physical_picture: These sectors explain how the existing 4D action can be read in reduced atomic and lepton-like regimes. They should not be presented as completed full moving-throat PDE theorems.
Hydrogenic structure is a controlled zero-mode consequence; lepton half-integer structure remains conditional on a selective mixed-sector route and autonomous closure.
mathematical_core: The useful public split is reduced-sector theorem, conditional theorem, and open spin/discretizer gate. That split makes the pending work visible without hiding the structured progress.
Mass ledgers and Berry-rotor corridors should cite notes until a particle-sector paper exists.
status_note: This topic should produce backfill tags for atom, lepton, and lepton-mass note sources.

topics.title: Anomaly and g-2 common quotient corridor
topics.summary: The current anomaly story separates a staggered baseline from a conditional common quotient or prefactor-slope layer that still requires branch data.

physical_picture: The anomaly material should be presented as a sharp corridor, not as a closed prediction. The model identifies a common charge-inertia transport layer that would need the same branch machinery as other response packets.
That makes the g-2 page a useful reader bridge between particle-sector notes and the moving-throat branch exporter.
mathematical_core: The quotient coordinates and Xi1/P1/P0 bridge define the target language. They should be linked to the 5PN continuation and weak-axisymmetric packet pages.
The graph firewall prevents the common layer from being advertised as closed before the actual branch tangent is computed.
status_note: Treat this as notes-backed until the g-2 derivation ledger becomes a formal paper.

topics.title: Status firewalls: what the site must not overclaim
topics.summary: Status firewalls are public guardrails that block invalid upgrades such as projection equals reduction, local 4PN equals full tail closure, or g-2 already closed.

physical_picture: Firewalls are not bureaucracy. They are how the public site stays honest while summarizing a large derivation program.
A reader should be able to tell immediately which results are exact, which are conditional, and which are open branch targets.
mathematical_core: The graph represents invalid inferences as explicit nodes and negative queries. Public topic pages should surface the relevant firewall wherever a tempting shortcut exists.
This also gives future papers a checklist: closing a gate means changing graph status with source support, not editing prose alone.

topics.title: Future paper worklist
topics.summary: Notes-only material is intentionally visible and tagged so it can be backfilled with formal paper citations once new papers are published.

physical_picture: This page is the maintenance bridge between the reader website and the research queue. It is acceptable for public pages to discuss notes-backed material if they clearly say that no formal paper exists yet.
When a new paper is published, the source graph should be updated first; then this site can regenerate and remove or shrink the pending badge automatically.
mathematical_core: A pending source is any graph source marked `future_paper_needed`, `future_paper_note`, or located only under `notes/` without a research paper DOI.
The generator exports `atlas/exports/future_paper_backfill.yaml` so Codex can find every topic and node that needs citation cleanup after publication.
